description: We are a team of students from CECyT 16 "Hidalgo" IPN, who are passionate about space, technology and new challenges. Our team is ready to give our best to solve the challenge we chose to take on.
summary:
Do you remember Buzz Lightyear’s wrist communicator? What if we used a wrist-mounted console that helps us explore Mars?
In science fiction, astronauts commonly use wrist devices to communicate, check maps, and spot environmental hazards. In reality, it is not recommended to use electronic wrist displays because the space suit makes their use unconventional and uncomfortable
Today, Didelphis team presents the Martian Wrist-Mounted Console, designed to explore Gale Crater, which has a variety of geophysical, radiological, and atmospheric hazards.
Using real NASA data from Gale Crater, our device uses side buttons and an OLED display. Built on an Arduino for the prototype, its reinforced protective casing shields the internal microcontroller from Martian dust and radiation. It also uses physical audio and light alarms to warn astronauts of immediate zone dangers and guide them safely toward the nearest safe zone.
details:
The Martian Map Wrist-Mounted Console is a device that works with a microcontroller. The purpose of this prototype is to be small and useful for explorers who can't hold bulky devices during their travel in Gale Crater.

It is a simple device that centres on showing a map with the 8 different locations of Gale Crater, along with environmental information of each one. During an explorer's travel, the wrist console can detect through sensors whether the radiation, atmospheric or geophysic conditions are appropriate or if the astronaut must go back to a safe zone.
